Hi,

Thanks for reaching out, and sorry for the trouble with Outlook running slow after the recent update.

To get this resolved quickly, here are a few initial steps to try, along with some info we'll need if the issue persists:

Quick things to try first:
1. Restart Outlook fully (close it via Task Manager if it's hanging, then reopen).
2. Restart your computer if you haven't since the update - this clears out any lingering update processes still running in the background.
3. Disable hardware graphics acceleration: File > Options > Advanced > uncheck "Disable hardware graphics acceleration" (try toggling this either way).
4. Check for add-ins that may be conflicting: File > Options > Add-ins > Manage "COM Add-ins" > Go, then disable any non-essential add-ins and restart Outlook.
5. Run Outlook in Safe Mode (Windows key + R, type "outlook /safe") to see if performance improves - this helps us isolate whether an add-in or the profile is the cause.

Details that will help us dig deeper if the above doesn't fix it:
- Is this happening with a specific action (searching, opening emails, switching folders) or general sluggishness throughout?
- Approximately how large is your mailbox / how many items are in your Inbox?
- Are you using Outlook in Cached Exchange Mode?
- Which Outlook/Office build number are you on now (File > Office Account > About Outlook)?
- Did this start immediately after the update, and is it affecting other apps or just Outlook?

We'll continue investigating on our end as well (checking for known issues with the recent update build), and will follow up shortly. In the meantime, if any of the steps above help, please let us know so we can close this out.

Thanks for your patience,
Service Desk

To help us triage, could you confirm the following:
1. Which Outlook version/build are you on now (File > Office Account > About Outlook)?
2. Is this happening on one machine or multiple?

5. Approximate size of your mailbox/OST file, if known.

In the meantime, here are a few quick things that often resolve slowness right after an Outlook update:

- Restart Outlook fully (and reboot the machine if you haven't since the update).
- Run Outlook in Safe Mode (hold Ctrl while launching Outlook) to see if add-ins are the cause. If it's fast in Safe Mode, an add-in is likely the culprit.
- Check for a paused/large OST rebuild: Outlook can be slow for a while after an update while it re-indexes or migrates data in the background — this can take some time on larger mailboxes and usually resolves on its own within a few hours.
- Verify Windows Search indexing status (Control Panel > Indexing Options) — if Outlook is still being indexed, search and folder switching will be slow temporarily.
- Disable Cached Exchange Mode temporarily as a test (not a permanent fix, just to isolate the cause).

Once we have your answers above, we'll dig further (checking add-ins, OST health, and network/profile issues) and get this resolved.

Thanks for your patience,
IT Service Desk

I can expedite that approval but can't bypass it, even under time pressure — this protects the company (and the CEO) from unauthorized access claims later.

If this is simply about pulling numbers for the board meeting, in most setups a standard/report-viewer role is sufficient and I can enable that right away once I have the username — no admin escalation needed.

Please reply with:
- The exact account/username having trouble
- Whether the goal is just to view/pull reports (likely no admin needed) or to manage the reporting tool's configuration (admin needed, requires approval)
